title: Felix — quant probe daily scratchpad
content:
2026-03-10 / quick daily log - sprint probe

Goal: short-cycle experiments to see quality/latency tradeoffs when moving 7B family from FP16 -> 4-bit PTQ with KV-cache active. Main questions: does prefix caching amplify quantization artifacts? can we keep <120ms token latency at batch=1 on A100-80?

Summary so far:
- Models: base-open-7b (fp16), base-open-7b-ptq4 (4-bit PTQ, GPTQ-style), base-open-7b-ptq4-opt (per-channel fine-tune-ish).
- HW: local dev node (A100-80GB), dedicated staging pool (pool-d-staging-3, 2xA100x80).
- Runtime: serve:dev with batcher disabled for single-token tests; kv-cache=on (cold/warm)

Quick commands I used:
- run single-step generation (cold cache):
  curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/generate -d '{"model":"base-open-7b-ptq4","prompt":"Explain memcached in one sentence","max_tokens":64}' | jq -r .output
- start eval harness (small eval set): python tools/eval_small.py --model base-open-7b-ptq4 --prompts eval/rlhf-small-v1.json --out tmp/ptq4-run.json

Observations / raw numbers (avg of 10 runs):
- fp16 (batch=1, cold): 95ms/token, 370 tokens/sec sustained; top-p sampling; latency tail (95p) ~180ms
- ptq4 (batch=1, cold): 110ms/token, 320 tokens/sec; 95p ~240ms
- ptq4-opt (batch=1, cold): 102ms/token, 340 tokens/sec; 95p ~200ms
- warm cache reduces latency by ~18-25% across configs (less for ptq4), but note: ptq4 shows slightly higher variance with cache hits >80%

Quality signals (spot checks on 200 eval prompts):
- automated metric: BLEU-ish/overlap isn't great for open prompts, but classifier-based QA accuracy drop ~3.4% fp16->ptq4, 1.4% fp16->ptq4-opt
- hallucination cases: short factual queries show small artifact: numbers rounding or unit errors (e.g., 5GB -> 5120MB -> reported as 5.12GB), more frequent in raw ptq4
- prompt-sensitivity: instruction-following tends to degrade slightly with ptq4 but recoverable by temperature lowering and higher repetition penalty

Hypothesis: quantization noise interacts with cached KV entries because rounding errors accumulate in long-prefix attention. ptq4-opt (with per-channel fudge) mitigates but not fully.

Mini prompt set I used (examples):
- "Summarize in two bullets: {context}"
- "Q: {question}\nA:"  (short-answer, few-shot 2 examples)
- "Given this API spec, list 3 edge cases not covered: {spec}"

Notable failures (examples saved to tmp/ptq4-errors.txt):
- Prompt: 'Convert 1.2 TB to MB' -> fp16: '1228800 MB' (correct); ptq4: '1,228,800 MB' (formatting noise, ok); ptq4 sometimes returns '1.2e6 MB' (bad for parsing downstream).
- Long prefix repetition: a 512-token prompt with code comments yields repeated last line on ptq4 in 4/50 runs.

Next actions / TODOs:
- [ ] Run batch=4 and batch=8 latency/throughput curve for all variants (to see amortization for live workloads)
- [ ] Re-run with runtime kv-cache disabled to measure pure decode noise baseline (isolate cache effect)
- [ ] Add small calibration pass (per-layer scale adjust) for ptq4-opt and re-run 1k eval prompts
- [ ] Add quick A/B to routing policy in staging: route 5% traffic to ptq4-opt with fallback to fp16 on regressions
- [ ] Share a short note with SRE/Serving about observed tail variance -> possible autoscale tweak (ticket JIRA-OPS-451)

Signals to capture in Redwood Console (manual list to add):
- token-latency distribution per model-variant, per-prefix-length bucket (0-64,65-256,256+)
- kv-cache hit ratio vs. lat/quality delta
- error/hallucination classifier score by quantization variant

Random dev notes and reminders:
- Try different random seeds on ptq4-opt; variance seems seed-sensitive.
- Check PR #432 for reproduced quantization script; I locally patched a clamping bug (line ~87) that helped reduce one-off large tokens.
- Ask Maya to run eval harness on staging cluster overnight (she's ok with this)

Quick log entry (2026-03-11 morning):
- Left off: calibration code half-finished, test harness queued on staging, current baseline: ptq4-opt promising but needs more runs.

End of scratchpad. Will update after batch runs and calibration.
